absent: Implementation of crash_exclude_mem_range and crash_mem allocation outside the test driver.
Binary layout and alignment of struct range and struct crash_mem.
Locking and concurrency rules for global key_count, keys_header, address, reuse and restore flags.
Full configfs attribute wiring and permission bits for description, count, reuse and restore.
Behavior of arch protect and unprotect helpers and old memory read path including encryption handling.
Keyring lookup, creation, serial handling and quota semantics.
Boot parameter name bound to the setup routine and kdump kernel detection.
Segment limits, page size, alignment constants and memory hole selection for kexec buffers.

findings.text: Weak accessor exposes previously stored key bytes from old memory at a caller supplied position while honoring platform memory encryption status.
Loader places the assembled key header into a kexec buffer and records resulting address and size in the image, doing nothing when no keys are configured.
Buffer helper appends a new segment to a file mode kexec image after aligning sizes and locating a suitable memory hole.
Two global resources reserve crash kernel memory, both initially empty and marked busy system RAM with crash kernel descriptor.
Test descriptor associates a label with an interval to exclude, initial capacity and initial interval set, expected interval set, and expected status.
Stored key entry keeps a length field plus a fixed size descriptor area plus a fixed size opaque payload area.
Header aggregates a total count with a trailing variable length array of key entries whose length is governed by that count.
Configuration object pairs generic configfs item storage with an optional dynamically allocated description string.

Exclusion intervals are inclusive on both ends; strictly disjoint or merely touching intervals leave stored data unchanged, partial overlap trims the edge inward past the excluded bound, full covering removes the stored interval, interior exclusion splits one interval into two with a gap around the excluded span.

Single point exclusion behaves as a one unit inclusive interval: outside points preserve the interval, endpoint points trim one unit, interior points split into two intervals excluding only that point.
When interior exclusion would need an extra slot but capacity is exhausted, the operation reports out of memory and preserves the original interval count.
Test driver builds isolated memory from initial parameters, invokes exclusion, checks status first, then on success checks the full interval set and on failure checks that count is unchanged.
Excluding the low megabyte clears three adjacent low intervals entirely, and a split spanning multiple intervals without spare capacity fails and leaves all intervals unchanged.
Serialized header size grows with configured key count to hold the count plus that many entries.

Header construction iterates only matching child items, requires a description for each, copies the descriptor with a bounded copy and resolves payload from the logon store, aborting on first failure.
Payload extraction holds the target key read semaphore while checking revocation state and copying data, releasing on all paths and dropping the reference after.
Subsystem mutex is initialized during module init before registration to serialize later configfs access.
Key count increments on successful item creation and decrements on item release; creation beyond the configured maximum is rejected.
Reuse flag defaults false; enabling it requires an existing crash image with a stored address, then reloads the header from reserved memory with temporary unprotect and reprotect.
Restore flag triggers a one time transfer of stored keys into the thread user keyring on first write while false, then records the requested boolean value.
Init selects a kdump personality with a restore only view when running as kdump kernel, otherwise the normal keys view, then initializes the group and registers the subsystem with cleanup on failure.
Early boot parameter parser converts the supplied string to a numeric address, accepting only inputs that consume characters, otherwise clearing the address and reporting invalid argument.
Unit suite registers two cases covering a single interval matrix and historical regressions, iterating over table entries and logging each label.
User keyring restoration looks up a writable user keyring, reads the count from old memory, allocates and reads the full header, then creates or updates one user key per entry.
Description update rejects empty input and overlong input beyond the allowed length, frees the old string only after validation, and reports allocation failure distinctly.
Restore path validates the retrieved count against the maximum before allocation and aborts without allocating when excessive.
Logon payload longer than the maximum is rejected without copying, and revoked or missing payload is reported distinctly.
Buffer addition refuses non file mode images, segment table exhaustion, and any addition after control pages exist, warning in the latter case.
Creation guard uses a strictly greater than comparison against the maximum, so a count already at the maximum still permits another allocation.
Maximum number of dm-crypt keys supported is 128.
Maximum size of one dm-crypt key payload is 256 bytes.
Maximum length of a dm-crypt key description is 128.
